prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet, single image, fully transparent background.

SUBJECT: the tall, heavily muscled African-American professional basketball
player in the attached reference image. Match that character exactly, his face
above all: dark brown skin, a shaved head, a broad, full, rounded face with
full cheeks, a heavy brow, a broad nose and full lips, exactly as the reference
draws them. He is easy-going and good-humoured -- a star playing on easy mode
against easy opponents, relaxed, amused and enjoying himself, with a confident
half-smile as his resting expression, never a scowl. Heavy shoulders and arms,
a blue sleeveless basketball jersey with a yellow number 34, blue shorts with
white and yellow trim, white high-top sneakers with blue and yellow flashes
over white socks. Identical colours, identical proportions, identical build and
identical height as the reference, in every frame.

LAYOUT: one horizontal row of 6 frames of equal width, evenly spaced. No
borders, no frame numbers, no labels, no background, no drop shadows.

POSE GUIDE: TWO images are attached, and they do different jobs.

The COLOUR image of the character is the only authority on WHO HE IS. His
colours, his proportions, his build, his height, his face, his kit and the
drawing style all come from that image and from the SUBJECT above, and nothing
below changes any of them. It does NOT decide which way he faces: in that
drawing he is turned toward the right edge, and in this sheet he faces the
viewer squarely.

The other image is a POSE GUIDE: a stick figure on a white background, standing
in a row on one ground line, in the same left-to-right order as the FRAMES
listed below. The Nth figure in the pose guide is the pose for the Nth frame.
Take the GEOMETRY from it and only the geometry: where each foot stands on the
ground line, how deeply the knees are bent, how low the shoulders and head are,
and where the elbows and hands are. Where the words below and the pose guide
describe the same thing, they agree; the pose guide is the exact version of it.

THE COLOURS ON THE POSE GUIDE name the limbs: the RED arm and the ORANGE leg
are on the VIEWER'S RIGHT, the BLUE arm and the GREEN leg on the viewer's left.
The two arms do DIFFERENT things wherever the pose guide draws them
differently.

THE HANDS ON THE POSE GUIDE: a small rounded square is a clenched FIST. A
narrow shape pointing down is an open hand, fingers down. A broad paddle with
spread fingers is an OPEN hand.

THE HEAD ON THE POSE GUIDE: the small TRIANGLE is his nose and the two small
ovals on either side of the head are his ears. With the triangle in the middle
of the face he looks straight at the viewer; moved to one side, he has turned
his head that way. The upright line down the face marks its centre and the
level line his eyes. His head is shaved smooth, so the pose guide draws no hair
on it. A head with NO face lines and no triangle, only an oval on each side, is
hanging so far forward and down that we see only the TOP of his shaved head and
not his face.

Draw the character from the colour reference standing in those positions. The
pose guide is an instruction, not artwork: its thin lines, its colours, its
joint dots, its white background, its circular head, its triangle and its ovals
are NOT part of the drawing and must not appear anywhere in it.

CAMERA: locked off. Identical distance and eye level in every frame. The
character must be exactly the same height in every frame, and the same height
as in the reference image — do not zoom, crop, recompose or rescale between
frames. All frames share one ground line: the soles of both feet touch the same
horizontal line in every frame, and the feet stay planted throughout.

VIEW: front view, facing the viewer.

He has just sunk a shot and has turned to the crowd to get them on their feet
-- both arms up with the palms turned upward, scooping the noise higher,
looking from one side of the room to the other. Delighted, and completely in
charge of the building. Frames 2 to 6 are one continuous move.

FRAMES, left to right:
1. CALIBRATION POSE: standing straight upright, feet shoulder-width apart, arms
   hanging relaxed at his sides, facing the viewer, in the plain neutral
   standing pose from the reference image. This exact pose appears as the first
   frame of every sheet in this set and must be drawn identically every time.
2. Standing up tall out of his stance, both arms lifting out wide to shoulder
   height with the palms turned UP and open, head turned to the VIEWER'S LEFT
   toward the crowd, broad grin.
3. The first scoop: both hands driven UP above his head, palms still turned up,
   elbows nearly straight, chin lifted, mouth open in a shout.
4. Both hands dropped back down to chest height, palms still turned up and
   open, elbows tucked in, head swinging round to the VIEWER'S RIGHT to take in
   the other side of the room.
5. The second scoop: both hands driven UP again and higher, arms straight, head
   back, roaring up at the crowd.
6. Arms coming back down and out to his sides with the palms still open, chin
   up, an enormous satisfied grin, easing back into a low athletic stance.

This is a one-shot, not a loop. Frame 2 is the moment the ball drops through
the net; frame 6 is where he comes to rest.

The two raised positions must be clearly and obviously higher than the two low
ones -- the up-and-down travel of the arms is the whole gesture, and if the
frames differ only a little the move reads as standing still.

STYLE: VGA-era 256-colour DOS-game pixel art, drawn pixel by pixel — NOT a
modern illustration with a pixel filter over it. The limits below are the look;
keep all of them: - At most THREE tones per material: a base, one darker
shadow, one lighter highlight. Hard edges between the tones. - NO gradients, NO
soft or airbrushed shading, NO glow, NO bloom, and NO anti-aliasing anywhere —
not on the outline, not between tones, not around the silhouette. - Where a
tone change needs softening, use visible ORDERED DITHER — a checkerboard of the
two tones. Dither, never blend. - Chunky square pixels on one consistent grid,
plainly visible at full size. - A bold dark outline around the silhouette and
around the major forms inside it. The background must be fully transparent
(alpha 0) with no haze, glow or soft fringe around the silhouette. Output a
wide landscape image.

The character is NOT holding a basketball in any frame — the ball is drawn
separately by the game.
